title: Ordinary completed-ring recollement realizes the integral operations
statement:
Fix a field $k$, a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites and the coefficient categories $D^b_c(T,A_n)$ and $D^b_c(T,R)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], for $T=X,Z,U$.
Put $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $u^*_{\rm ord}$ and $Rf_{*,\rm ord}$ for ordinary derived operations on $B_T$-module sheaves, and $u^*_{\rm comp},Rf_*$ for the specified integral operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image]. For $u=i,j$, the canonical ordinary-to-completed pullback comparison is invertible on derived-complete objects. For $f=i,j$ and $K\in D^b_c(\operatorname{dom} f,R)$ the strict-tower direct-image comparison is an isomorphism
$$Rf_{*,\rm ord}K\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_{*,n}K_n=Rf_*K,\qquad K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_T}(A_n)_T.$$
There are also canonical isomorphisms $(Rf_*K)_n\cong Rf_{*,n}K_n$ and $(u^*_{\rm comp}K)_n\cong u_n^*K_n$ in the actual finite module categories. These comparisons preserve the finite projections, quotient transitions, completion units, and the ordinary pullback/direct-image adjunction units and counits. Both pullbacks and both direct images preserve the precise integral constructible category, with one finite cohomological interval for all reductions of each image. The ambient completed-ring kernel adjoint $Ri^!_0$ of [lem-sf-ringed-closed-kernel-adjoint] restricts to this category, and for every $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ the ambient distinguished supported triangle $i_*Ri^!_0K\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to i_*Ri^!_0K[1]$, whose first two arrows are the exceptional counit and the open unit, lies in $D^b_c(X,R)$ and has the specified integral $i_*,j^*,Rj_*$ and their adjunction maps. In particular $i^*i_*\cong1$, $j^*Rj_*\cong1$, $j^*i_*=0$, and $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P[m],Rj_*G)=0$ there. The restricted adjoint is $R$-linear and exact, with the shift structure induced by adjunction. A morphism of integral constructible objects is invertible whenever all its reductions are invertible. No identification of the two ambient constant-ring and completed-ring module categories is asserted.

source.place: Integral stage: ordinary operations, completion and ambient restriction; returned steps 5–6 and first part of 7, integral part of 9

proof.text: First verify the hypotheses of the completion and ringed-support tools. The valuation ring $R$ is a DVR with finite residue field; each $A_n$ is finite and has the augmented free resolution $[R\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}R]$. Thus $(R,(\varpi))$ is the Noetherian adic datum with finite perfect positive quotients. A field is Noetherian, so the finite-type scheme $X$ is Noetherian, and its open $U$ is Noetherian and quasi-compact; consequently $j$ is quasi-compact. A closed subscheme of a finite-type scheme over a field is again finite type, as follows on each affine chart by taking the quotient of a finitely generated algebra. The canonical coefficient isomorphisms $u^{-1}B_X\cong B_{\operatorname{dom}u}$, for $u=i,j$, commute with the finite projections and quotient transitions. All subsequent module operations use these isomorphisms.

source.place: Integral stage, coefficient datum and ordinary ringed realization; Stacks 09AA, 09BM hypotheses

proof.text: Apply the immersion comparison to $i$ and $j$. Ordinary pullback is exact inverse image and preserves derived completeness; the actual comparison $c_{u,K}:u^*_{\rm ord}K\to u^*_{\rm comp}K$ is invertible for every derived-complete $K$. The specified integral pullback is the same strict quotient-tower construction, not a newly chosen functor. Its finite-reduction comparison is an isomorphism in $D((A_n)_{\operatorname{dom}u})$ and identifies the finite projection, successive quotients and completion unit. On integral constructible objects the ordinary inverse image is constructible and every reduction remains in the input's single cohomological interval. The two completed pullbacks are compared on one strict tower. Since $u^*$ is exact (identified coefficients), it is computed termwise, so the derived tower pullback of the reduction tower of a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ is represented by the strict tower $\operatorname{Res}_nu_n^*(P\otimes_{B_X}(A_n)_X)$, which is also the tower defining the specified integral pullback. Countable products of pro-etale module sheaves are exact, so the natural Roos isomorphism $\rho:\mathsf C\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim$ between the product-cone model and the total derived limit of this tower applies. It commutes with every projection and carries the cone lift of the quotient augmentation to the canonical derived map. Thus $c_{u,K}$ followed by $\rho^{-1}$ is the comparison into the specified integral pullback, with the same projections and completion unit.

source.place: Integral stage, pullback comparison and reduction normalization

proof.text:
Use the canonical quotient reconstruction of a complete complex $K$. The Roos-triangle completeness convention in the item agrees with invertibility of the canonical quotient augmentation and with intrinsic Koszul completeness. For $f=i,j$, apply the ringed direct-image/limit theorem to this augmentation. It gives
$$d_{f,K}:Rf_{*,\rm ord}K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_{*,n}K_n.$$
The right side, including its quotient-induced transitions, is exactly the specified integral $Rf_*K$. The comparison is the derived comparison of $f_*\lim=\lim f_*^{\rm Tow}$, on K-injective strict towers. It therefore respects each finite projection and all transitions before evaluation; it is not an inference that equal evaluated maps must be equal. The same theorem proves completeness of the ordinary image and identifies its completion unit with direct image of the input augmentation followed by this comparison. The terms of $Rf_*^{\rm Tow}K_\bullet$ are $Rf_{*,\rm ord}\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$. The natural ring-change comparison $d_n:\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{*,n}K_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,\rm ord}\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$ for $\pi_n$ applies with the isomorphisms $c_f,c_{f,n}$ of step 1, as $\pi_nc_f=c_{f,n}f^{-1}\pi_n$. On a K-injective $(A_n)$-complex $J$ it is the underived identity $f_*\operatorname{Res}_nJ=\operatorname{Res}_nf_*J$ followed by a resolution, as is the transition identification of the integral direct image for $A_{n+1}\to A_n$. Resolving $\operatorname{Res}J$ first over $A_{n+1}$ and then over $B$, the composition normalization of derived pushforwards gives $d_n=d_{n+1}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}(\text{transition identification})$. So the $d_n$ form a tower isomorphism, and $d_{f,K}$ lands in the specified tower with its transitions.

source.place: Integral stage, ordinary direct image and strict quotient reconstruction; Stacks sites-cohomology.tex 0A07 and proetale.tex 099N

proof.text: The finite direct-image map used here is the scalar-extension adjunct of the $n$-th limit projection, as in the definition of the integral direct image. The complete-direct-image reduction theorem says this very adjunct is invertible in the actual finite module category, for any chosen Roos presentation of the prescribed tower. Equivalently the projection-formula comparison of the direct-image/limit theorem gives $(Rf_{*,\rm ord}K)\otimes^L_{B_X}(A_n)_X\cong Rf_{*,n}K_n$. Under $d_{f,K}$ these are the specified reduction maps, with their quotient transitions and completion normalization. Together with step 2 this supplies both asserted families of finite-category isomorphisms.

source.place: Integral stage, finite projection adjuncts in their module categories

proof.text:
Retain the ordinary derived adjunction $u^*_{\rm ord}\dashv Ru_{*,\rm ord}$. Its restriction to complete objects, followed by completion of the left functor, has Hom bijection given by precomposition with $c_{u,M}$ and the ordinary Hom bijection. The completion-reflector theorem and quotient/Koszul comparison identify this reflector with the specified quotient-tower completion; the preceding completeness equivalence identifies its complete objects. Hence the reflector adjunction formulas give
$$\eta^c_M=Ru_{*,\rm ord}(c_{u,M})\eta^{\rm ord}_M,\qquad
\varepsilon^c_Nc_{u,Ru_{*,\rm ord}N}=\varepsilon^{\rm ord}_N.$$
Conjugate the right functor by $d_{u,N}$ from step 3. These formulas identify both integral unit and counit with the ordinary ones under the specified comparisons. At the coefficient and strict-tower level the completed-coefficient direct-image diagram theorem retains the quotient units, evaluation squares and universal-unit normalization; its finite evaluations are the ordinary finite adjunction maps. Thus the identification includes the finite projections and quotient adjunction maps, rather than just endpoints of adjunctions.

source.place: Integral stage, ordinary adjunction maps under completion and strict-system realization

proof.text: For $f=i,j$ use integral direct-image constructibility, which applies to finite-type morphisms over any field with $\ell$ invertible, without an algebraic-closedness assumption. It states completeness, constructibility of every $Rf_{*,n}K_n$, and one common cohomological interval for these reductions. In particular $Rj_*j^*K$ and $i_*P$ are integral constructible. Through $d_f$ this proves the same assertion for the ordinary images. The corresponding pullback assertions, with the unchanged interval, were proved in step 2. No replacement by a finite-Tor category is made.

source.place: Integral stage, preservation and uniform boundedness

proof.text: The uniformity can also be read directly along the blueprint's induction, so finite-level boundedness is not mistaken for uniform boundedness. Put $M_n=Rf_{*,n}K_n$ and choose an interval $[a_f,b_f]$ for $M_1$, which exists by step 6. Tensor the coefficient sequence $0\to A_1\xrightarrow{\varpi^{n-1}}A_n\to A_{n-1}\to0$ with one flat-term K-flat $B$-representative of $K$. Exact derived tensor and the short-exact-complex triangle give a triangle of restricted $B$-complexes $K_1\to K_n\to K_{n-1}\to K_1[1]$. Apply exact ordinary derived direct image; the ring-change comparisons $d_1,d_n,d_{n-1}$ of step 3 identify its terms with the restricted finite images. The resulting triangle has vertices the restrictions of $M_1,M_n,M_{n-1}$. Its cohomology long exact sequence proves by induction that every $M_n$ vanishes outside $[a_f,b_f]$. Each $M_n$ is constructible by step 6, so this verifies precisely the uniform-interval condition of the item.

source.place: Integral stage, triangles from successive coefficient quotients and induction on n

proof.text:
Work now on the ambient unbounded $B$-module derived categories. The ringed kernel-adjoint theorem supplies $i_*\dashv Ri^!_0$, $i^*\dashv i_*$, $j^*\dashv Rj_*$, and the actual isomorphisms $i^*i_*\cong1$, $j^*Rj_*\cong1$ and vanishing $j^*i_*=0$. For any ambient $P,G$ and integer $m$, its adjunction gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P[m],Rj_*G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j^*i_*P[m],G)=0.$$
In particular this holds on the full constructible categories after steps 2–6 and preserves the units and counits of step 5.

source.place: Vanishing and integral stage, ringed ambient adjunctions

proof.text: Complete the actual ordinary open unit $K\to Rj_*j^*K$ to an ambient distinguished triangle $F\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to F[1]$ by TR1 and rotation. Apply $j^*$, exact as a termwise exact module functor; the image of its middle arrow is invertible, since its composite with the invertible open counit is the identity by the triangle identity. The cohomology long exact sequence gives $j^*F=0$. On each cohomology sheaf $H^r(F)$ the supported closed-unit theorem now applies. Since $i^*,i_*$ are exact, their cohomology comparisons identify $H^r(F\to i_*i^*F)$ with that supported sheaf unit. All these maps are invertible, so the unbounded cohomology criterion proves $F\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*i^*F$. This ambient support argument imposes no boundedness on $F$ or on $Ri^!_0K$.

source.place: Integral stage, construct the ambient open-unit fibre and identify closed support

proof.text:
Apply the orthogonal-counit triangle theorem with its fully faithful left adjoint equal to ambient $i_*$, right adjoint $Ri^!_0$, middle vertex $K$, and last vertex $Rj_*j^*K$. Step 9 places $F$ in the essential image of $i_*$, and step 8 gives the required orthogonality in every shift. The theorem replaces the first map of that triangle by the actual counit, while retaining its second map, the actual open unit. It yields the ambient distinguished triangle
$$i_*Ri^!_0K\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_i}K\xrightarrow{\eta_j}Rj_*j^*K\longrightarrow i_*Ri^!_0K[1].$$
Full faithfulness used here follows from the invertible counit $i^*i_*\cong1$: the adjunction Hom bijection followed by that counit is inverse to applying $i_*$ on Hom sets.

source.place: Integral stage, supported triangle with the actual exceptional counit and open unit

proof.text: For integral constructible $K$, steps 2 and 6 put $K$ and $Rj_*j^*K$ in the integral constructible subcategory. This is a full triangulated subcategory, so the first vertex $i_*Ri^!_0K$ of step 10 belongs to it. Apply its ordinary $i^*$, which preserves that category by step 2. The invertible closed counit identifies the result with $Ri^!_0K$. Thus the ambient adjoint restricts, the entire supported triangle lies in the precise integral category, and fullness restricts the original Hom adjunction without changing its maps. Steps 2–5 identify its displayed $i_*,j^*,Rj_*$ and maps with the specified integral ones.

source.place: Integral stage, restrict the ambient kernel adjoint and triangle

proof.text: The restricted $i_*$ is exact: ambient closed direct image is the exact termwise module functor, and the integral subcategories carry their inherited distinguished triangles. It is $R$-linear because on a section $x$ direct image retains $r x$ as $r$ times the retained section; this equality descends through complexes and localization and the comparisons of steps 3–5. The linear-right-adjoint theorem therefore makes the restricted $Ri^!_0$ additive and $R$-linear. Equip it with the unique adjunction-induced coherent shift structure supplied by the adjunction-shift theorem. Its unit and counit are shift compatible with this structure. Apply the triangulated-right-adjoint theorem to exact $i_*$: the restricted adjoint is exact with precisely this shift structure.

source.place: Integral part of consequences, linearity and the adjunction-induced exact structure

proof.text: Finally let $v:K\to L$ be a morphism in the integral category with every finite reduction invertible. Complete it to a cone triangle; the cone $C$ is again integral constructible, by triangulated closure. Exact derived change of rings and its cohomology long exact sequence show $C_n=0$ for every $n$. The defining Roos completeness triangle for $C$ then has both product vertices zero. Its cohomology long exact sequence gives $H^r(C)=0$ for every $r$, so $C=0$ by the unbounded cohomology criterion; the cone triangle similarly makes every $H^r(v)$ invertible, hence $v$ invertible. This uses only reconstruction within $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$, and never equates that ambient category with the one over the constant $R$-sheaf.

source.place: Integral stage, reduction conservativity by the complete cone
